applicant_utility.summary: TU Wien's own scholarships are modest one-off merit payments rather than study funding: the standard merit scholarship pays €750-€1,500 once a year, decided case by case by your Dean of Studies, so you still have to cover the €726.72-per-semester non-EU tuition fee and Vienna's living costs yourself. Eligibility is the catch for newcomers, because the state-backed merit and funding grants require EEA citizenship or five years of residence in Austria, so a first-year international from outside the EEA should run a parallel search on OeAD's grants.at database. If you are a woman admitted to an English-language Computer Science master's programme, the Helmut Veith Stipend at €6,000 a year plus a tuition fee waiver (deadline 30 November) is the one award that materially changes the economics.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled TU Wien students with EEA citizenship or 5+ years of Austrian residence who can document a strong ECTS record by mid-October, and female applicants to English-language CS master's programmes.
application_readiness_checklist: Order your Transcript of Records early and make sure it covers 01.10.-30.09. and includes negative grades - missing records are the most common failure point
Download forms F-990 and F-990d or your faculty's own form plus the information sheet from the dean's office page
Check the call's weighted minimum average grade and your § 18/§ 19 entitlement period before investing time in the application
For a funding grant, prepare the project description, cost breakdown, financing plan and cost offers, and secure your supervisor's expert opinion first
Book an appointment or email your dean's office, submit by 15 October and expect a decision around mid-December
Non-EEA newcomers should search grants.at in parallel for OeAD awards aimed at students coming from abroad
common_rejection_risks: Sending the file to the central university instead of your own faculty's dean's office, which runs its own call
A Transcript of Records that misses the 01.10.-30.09. window or omits negative grades
Falling below the weighted minimum average grade set in that year's call, or exceeding the § 18 entitlement period without a § 19 acknowledgment
Treating the award as reliable income - it is a one-off payment with no legal entitlement and limited numbers
Waiting on the 15 October round and missing the separate Helmut Veith (30 November) and completion-of-studies (October-November) windows
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees (€726.72 per semester for non-EU nationals plus the ÖH fee), living costs, accommodation, travel and health insurance - none of these are covered by the merit or funding grants.
document_audit: Transcripts must include negative grades and document the 01.10.-30.09. academic-year window in full
Records of studies from other universities need the matching recognition notifications attached
Non-EU applicants must attach the residence permit and the registration form for non-Austrian residence
Funding-grant budgets must be evidenced with cost estimates, and the Informatics call asks for at least two offers
alerts: The 15 October deadline lands days after the winter semester starts, so assemble transcripts during September
State scholarships are closed to non-EEA students without five years of Austrian residence, so plan on OeAD awards or self-funding from day one
The Helmut Veith Stipend closes 30 November and is restricted to female students of English-taught CS master's programmes
Never count this award as proof of funds for a visa or residence permit, given limited numbers and no legal entitlement
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the call's application form, attach the full transcript package, and hand it to your dean's office in person by appointment or by e-mail before 15 October; the dean notifies decisions around mid-December.

applicant_utility.summary: Webster Vienna's scholarship money is a tuition discount rather than a living allowance: bachelor's awards run €4,000-€12,000 a year and master's awards €3,000-€8,000, with the balance of tuition still owed by you, so you need separate proof of funds for living costs before the visa stage. Admission comes first, because you can only apply once you hold an acceptance letter to a full degree programme, and only about 20 new students win an award each year. The decisive ingredients are a 3.0+ GPA, documented financial need and a 1,000-1,200-word essay, so treat the essay and the financial evidence pack as the real application instead of a formality.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Admitted full-degree students with a GPA of at least 3.0, demonstrable financial need and solid English (B2 minimum, C1 for the top level) who can file inside the Spring round's 30 November 13:00 CET cutoff.

Request the online scholarship form from admissions@webster.ac.at at the start of the round rather than in its final week

Draft the essay to exactly 1,000-1,200 words on one of the two published prompts and check it against the criteria of the level you are targeting
Submit before 13:00 CET on 30 November (Spring round) or 31 May (Fall round) and confirm receipt with scholarship@webster.ac.at
Plan renewal from the first semester: full-time enrolment and a 3.0 semester GPA are conditions of keeping the award
common_rejection_risks: Applying before admission is complete - certificate and English preparation students are excluded outright
Submitting bank account statements, which are explicitly not accepted, instead of employer or pension confirmations of net earnings
Financial documents that are untranslated or quoted in another currency without the conversion rate
An essay outside the 1,000-1,200-word range or written on a topic other than the two published prompts
Missing the 13:00 CET cutoff, or dropping below full-time enrolment or a 3.0 GPA and losing renewal
Budgeting as if the award were a full ride when the remaining tuition stays your responsibility
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining tuition fee after a partial award, plus living costs, accommodation, health insurance and travel - Webster Vienna warns that students must arrange funding for travel and living costs for at least the first one to two months and that aid is not disbursed until studies begin.
